# Wyrd and Frith

The two load-bearing words of the world's metaphysics. Both are real Old
English/Norse terms, adopted by the author into canon (see `data/lexicon.yaml`).

## The Wyrd

> status: ratified (D-0048)

Pronounced like "weird"; Old English *wyrd*, "that which has come to pass" — the root
that gave Shakespeare his Weird Sisters. In this world the Wyrd is the living web of
cause and consequence binding soil, weather, beasts, and people. Not fate as prophecy:
fate as accumulated consequence. A healthy Wyrd is invisible and quiet. The study of
the Wyrd — generations deep, eventually religious in structure — is the intellectual
spine of the setting and of the narrator's own order ([[religion]], [[narrator]]).

### Working mechanics

> status: provisional (D-0072)

The session's model: the Wyrd behaves like a lawful, reactive fabric. Every taking and
giving is recorded in it. It can be reasoned with — that is what a spoken proof is —
and it cannot absorb contradiction indefinitely. Where false premises are imposed on
it (a fenced commons declared "separate," a dammed river declared "owned"), the
contradiction accumulates rather than dissipates.

## Frith

> status: ratified (D-0048)

Old English/Norse: peace, protection, right relation. The law of reciprocity — what is
taken must be balanced by what is returned. In the old cultures Frith was not
morality but physics-adjacent law: you take timber, you owe the wood. Sin, where the
word survives, means taking more than you return.

## Asking leave

> status: ratified (D-0146)

Frith has an everyday, diminutive form: asking leave. Entering a new place — a wood, a ford, a
strange valley — the native way is to ask the ground's leave and set down a small, freely given
gift, under the old rule that a gift closes no debt. The gift buys nothing and settles no
account; it opens a relationship and acknowledges that the ground is a party, never a thing.
This is the same consent law the hound's treaty runs on ([[animals]], D-0116) and the etiquette
the landvættir demand ([[anomalies]]), scaled down to a daily courtesy — and it is exactly what
tells native reciprocity apart from imperial trespass, which enters and takes as though the
ground owed it. The courtesy relates; it never compels, because a spirit made to obey is a
spirit no longer in treaty.

## Axiomatic debt

> status: provisional (D-0072)

The sickness mechanism, approved directionally across many exchanges: extraction
without reciprocity generates an accumulating imbalance — axiomatic debt. It sours
soil, breaks the order of seasons, curdles into [[anomalies]] — and it does
not go away when ignored. It is the world's carbon ledger, worn as pure fantasy: the
allegory stays beneath the floorboards (D-0030 discipline; never name it in modern
terms in-world).

## The sickness is systemic

> status: ratified (D-0007, D-0011, D-0013)

The world has a real sickness that manifests as many smaller animist spirit-problems —
the classic manga engine, rebuilt on Northern European animism. But the cause is never
a dark lord: the rich poisoned the world, and go on poisoning it, because the system
that enriches them requires it. Any given local horror traces upstream, through
watershed and tithe-roll, to somebody's hoard. The world is fucked, the ones who
fucked it live above the consequences, and removing them is the start — only the
start — of a fix.
